docs.title: Documentation
docs.description: Learn how to set up Daily Spark, track your habits, and keep a portable copy of your data.

sections.title: Start with one habit
sections.text: Open the Web App or install an available package. Create a habit, choose a schedule, and check in from Today. Review individual days and longer activity patterns in Progress.

sections.title: Organize your day
sections.text: Use collections for routines, notes for reflections, and the optional day planner for tasks alongside your habits. Settings keeps advanced preferences available without crowding Today.

sections.title: Keep your data with you
sections.text: Your records stay on this device by default. Export a backup before changing devices, uninstalling, or clearing browser storage. Inspect a backup before choosing Merge or Replace.

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.description: Set up Daily Spark and make your first check-in.

sections.title: 1. Choose where to use it
sections.text: Open the Web App in your browser, download the Android APK, or choose a Windows or Linux package from Download. The download page shows the available versions; macOS packages are not yet available.

sections.title: 2. Create a habit
sections.text: Use the + action and choose a habit. Give it a name, select an icon, and choose the schedule that fits your week. Start with a small action you can repeat.

sections.title: 3. Check in and review
sections.text: Mark a habit complete from Today. Open its details to review or edit a day, then use Progress and Calendar to see your activity over time.

sections.title: 4. Save a backup
sections.text: Open Settings ? Data & Backups and export your records. Keep a copy somewhere you control before uninstalling the app or clearing browser data.

sections.title: Updating Android
sections.text: Install the newer APK over the existing app when Android offers Update. Export a backup first. Avoid uninstalling to solve an update problem until you have saved your data.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Answers about accounts, offline use, supported devices, and your habit data.

backup-restore.title: Backup & restore
backup-restore.description: Save a portable copy of your habits and restore it with a preview before making changes.

sections.title: Export a backup
sections.text: Open Settings ? Data & Backups and choose an export. Use a full JSON backup to preserve records and history. Keep the file somewhere safe: ordinary backup files can contain your habits, notes, and settings.

sections.title: Inspect before restoring
sections.text: Select your backup in the restore flow. Review the preview before confirming. Merge combines the backup with existing records; Replace replaces the current data. Export your current data before using Replace.

sections.title: Encrypted transfers
sections.text: Where available, export an encrypted vault with your own passphrase, save or transfer the file, then import it on another device. This is a user-started transfer, rather than automatic cloud syncing. Keep the passphrase safe.

sections.title: Snapshots and folder backups
sections.text: Local snapshots stay on the device and do not protect you if its data is removed. Android also offers optional folder backups with daily or weekly scheduling. Keep a separate portable backup before uninstalling or resetting a device.

design-system.title: Design system
design-system.description: Quiet surfaces, warm accents, and clear actions. A visual guide to the product?s colors, typography, and rhythm.

sections.title: One clear primary action
sections.text: Warm Ember highlights the action that matters now. Secondary controls sit on quiet surfaces, with borders and spacing providing structure.

sections.title: Type with a purpose
sections.text: Display type establishes hierarchy, body text keeps instructions readable, and monospaced metrics make counts and dates easy to compare. Each app theme has its own complete type and color system.

sections.title: Space to breathe
sections.text: A four-pixel spacing rhythm keeps related items together. Rounded cards group content; generous touch targets and visible keyboard focus make controls easier to use.

sections.title: Motion with restraint
sections.text: Animation supports orientation and feedback. The website provides Pause motion, and the screenshot gallery keeps a separate pause control. Reduced-motion preferences are respected.

about.title: About Daily Spark
about.description: A free, local-first habit tracker built around one small action at a time.

sections.title: A quieter daily routine
sections.text: Daily Spark brings check-ins, schedules, progress, notes, and optional planning into one place. There are no leaderboards, ads, or required Daily Spark accounts.

sections.title: Local by default
sections.text: Your habit records live on your device. Optional exports let you choose when and how to move a backup. The website?s Privacy page explains storage and third-party links.

sections.title: Open source
sections.text: Daily Spark is published under the MIT License. Source code, issue discussions, and releases are hosted on GitHub and GitLab; the guides you need to use it are available here on the website.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: The project?s terms and conditions for using Daily Spark.

security.title: Security
security.description: How to protect your local records and report a security problem responsibly.

sections.title: Protect your device and backups
sections.text: Daily Spark keeps habit data local by default. Use your device?s security controls, keep the app updated, and store exported files safely. Only restore files you trust. A local snapshot is not a substitute for a separate backup.

sections.title: Report a vulnerability privately
sections.text: Use the project?s GitHub Security tab and choose Report a vulnerability if private reporting is available. Include the affected app version, device or browser, impact, and reproduction steps. Do not put exploit details or personal data in a public issue.

sections.title: What is in scope
sections.text: Reports concerning the Android app, Web App, local storage, backup and restore, and notification handling are relevant. Reports are reviewed on a best-effort basis; allow time for a fix before public disclosure.
